mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are adversely affected.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of periods with declining RSAFS, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% within a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with increasing GDPC1, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
